### Utility Functions

```{r}
# library(msa)
strict_consensus <- function(char_vec) {
  # Check if all character vectors have the same length
  if (!all(sapply(char_vec, function(x) nchar(x) == nchar(char_vec[1])))) {
    stop("All character vectors must have the same length.")
  }

  # Initialize an empty character vector to store the result
  result_sequence <- character(nchar(char_vec[1]))

  # Iterate over each position in the character vectors
  for (i in seq_len(nchar(char_vec[1]))) {
    # Get the characters at the current index for all vectors
    characters_at_position <- sapply(char_vec, function(x) substr(x, i, i))

    # Find the most common character at the current index
    most_common_char <- names(which.max(table(characters_at_position)))

    # Store 
    result_sequence[i] <- most_common_char
  }

  # Return
  return(paste(result_sequence, collapse = ""))
}

translate_DNA <- function(dna_data){
  clean_dna <- gsub("[^ACTG]", "", dna_data)
  DNA_strings <- Biostrings::DNAStringSet(clean_dna)
  translations <- as.character(Biostrings::translate(DNA_strings))
  return(translations)
}

#### Trim CDR3
trim_CDR3 <- function(seq_vec){
  return(substr(seq_vec, 2, nchar(seq_vec)-1))
}

top_groups <- function(results, clone_var){
  return(table(results[[clone_var]])[order(table(results[[clone_var]]), decreasing = T)])
}

## "Unrolling" duplicate values
unroll_dupes <- function(dat, unroll_column){
  # Create to store results
  result_vec <- vector()
  # Iterate over the duplicate count column
  for (i in 1:length(dat$duplicate_count)){
    result_vec <- c(result_vec, 
                    rep(dat[[unroll_column]],
                        each = dat$duplicate_count[i]))
  }
  return(result_vec)
}
```

# Pilot

For each clonal family in `{S19, S20, S21}` (S19 is 241 families- pick largest)
  Generate Consensus Sequence (for all n families)
  Search each other database (m) of k sequences
    (N x M) Matrix of Closest Clusters
      Each cell contain the COUNT of members within `X%` homology
        We can titrate the homology `{60, 70, 80, 85}`
        If there are identically-close families, aggregate them
        Bonus points: Consensus sequences too

## Strategy

1. Maintain all databases (with clones inferred) in a subdirectory of the `VHH/data/Cluster-DBs` folder

2. Maintain a `VHH/data/Cluster-DBs/results` folder for Cluster Databases

### Algorithm

```{r}
data_dir <- "~/VHH/data/Cluster-DBs"
res_dir <- "~/VHH/data/Cluster-DBs/results"

files <- list.files(data_dir)[grepl(".tsv", list.files(data_dir))]

consensus_clusters <- data.frame()
tmp_res <- data.frame()

# For each database file
for (f in files){
  
  dat <- read.csv(paste(data_dir, f, sep = '/'), header = T, stringsAsFactors = F, sep = '\t')
  
  cat("Loading file: ", f, '\n')
  # for each family in the database
  tab <- top_groups(dat, "clone_id")
  
  for (nm in names(tab)){
    # Subset the clones of interest
    tmp_frame <- dat[dat$clone_id == as.numeric(nm),]
    tmp_frame$junction_aa <- trim_CDR3(tmp_frame$junction_aa)
    cluster_id <- nm
    
    ## Note: here we need to ensure that we account for the 
    unrolled_CDR3s <- unroll_dupes(tmp_frame)
    
    consensus_sequence <- strict_consensus(unrolled_CDR3s)
    
    Dup_count <- sum(tmp_frame$duplicate_count)
    DNA_seqs_in_cluster <- length(unique(tmp_frame$sequence))
    CDR3s_in_cluster <- length(unique(tmp_frame$junction_aa))
    
    # Bind results
    tmp_res <- rbind(tmp_res, cbind(f,
                                    cluster_id,
                                    consensus_sequence,
                                    Dup_count,
                                    DNA_seqs_in_cluster,
                                    CDR3s_in_cluster))
    
  }
  
  cat("Completed file: ", f, '\n')
  file_out <- paste(res_dir, gsub('.tsv', '-consensuses26Feb24.csv', f), sep = '/')
  write.csv(tmp_res, file_out, row.names = F)
}
```
